# Vendor comparison

Vendor 1 is the provisional choice, provided it meets the required regional coverage and its integration effort does not outweigh the subscription savings. The available evidence supports a commercial preference, but not a final overall selection.

Vendors are numbered in the order of the supplied quotes. Figures use the supplied currency, which was not specified.

| Vendor | Annual quote | Two-year subscription total | Commitment supplied |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 40k | 80k | Not specified |
| 2 | 62k | 124k | Two years |
| 3 | 55k | 110k | Not specified |

Two-year totals assume unchanged annual rates and equivalent scope. Only Vendor 2 has a stated two-year commitment; the other totals are comparison scenarios, not confirmed contractual obligations. Taxes, implementation, usage charges and other fees were not supplied.

## Coverage

The first evaluation round recorded differences in regional coverage, but did not identify them by vendor. Confirm that each vendor supports every required region before selecting. A required coverage gap can rule out an otherwise attractive quote.

## Latency

All three meet the recorded latency bar. There is no supplied evidence that additional latency performance warrants a premium.

## Integration effort

One vendor requires substantially more integration work, but the notes do not identify which one. Obtain vendor-specific estimates for implementation, ongoing maintenance and delivery time.

Vendor 3 costs 15k more per year than Vendor 1, or 30k over two years. It makes sense if its additional coverage, reduced engineering effort or other demonstrated benefits justify that premium. For a one-off integration saving alone, the two-year break-even difference is 30k, assuming all other costs and benefits are equal.

Vendor 2 costs 22k more per year than Vendor 1, or 44k over two years. It also costs 7k more per year than Vendor 3, or 14k over two years, and requires a two-year commitment. It needs a demonstrated advantage over both alternatives to justify the premium and reduced ability to switch. The stated annual rate implies 124k across the term; payment timing and early-exit provisions remain unconfirmed.

## Recommendation and next steps

Proceed with Vendor 1 as the preferred candidate for validation. Choose Vendor 3 if the coverage and integration comparison demonstrates benefits worth its premium. Choose Vendor 2 only if it supplies a necessary capability or sufficient measurable benefit and the two-year term is acceptable.

Before a final selection, map coverage and integration effort to each vendor, confirm equivalent workload and service scope, and check implementation fees, usage allowances, support, renewal rates and cancellation terms. The existing workload-tier question remains unresolved, so confirm that each quote covers the intended workload. Project notes indicate legal review takes about ten working days; allow for that before signing.

This comparison uses the supplied quotes and existing project evaluation notes. No vendor-specific capability differences have been inferred.
